scenarios.title: The Other Foot
scenarios.text: The analyst shows him a statistic: ninety-two per cent of his touches are with his stronger foot. Opponents have noticed. They're showing him onto the other one every time.

choices.label: An hour extra every day for a month
choices.text: An hour a day against a wall with the wrong foot. By the end of the month he scores with it in training and the whole squad cheers.

choices.label: Play to your strengths
choices.desc: Be so good on one side it doesn't matter.
choices.text: He doubles down on his strong side. Some weeks it works. Some weeks a clever full-back shuts him down completely.

scenarios.title: The Goalkeeping Coach
scenarios.text: The goalkeeping coach wants to rebuild his technique: hand position, footwork, the way he sets himself before a shot. Six weeks of drills that will make him worse before they make him better.

choices.label: Commit fully
choices.text: Two awkward weeks, one howler in a match, then something clicks. He's a better keeper than he's ever been.

choices.label: Small tweaks only
choices.text: A few small changes. Nothing breaks. Nothing transforms either.

scenarios.title: The Heading Machine
scenarios.text: The club has bought a machine that fires balls at head height, a hundred an hour. The coach wants {J} on it every day. The physio is worried about how many headers that is.

choices.label: Use it, but limit the reps
choices.text: Twenty perfect headers a day. His timing in the air improves. His head stays clear.

choices.label: Go all in
choices.text: A hundred a day. His heading improves hugely. So do his headaches. The physio cuts it in half.

scenarios.title: Cross Until It Hurts
scenarios.text: The assistant coach has a challenge: hit a target zone with fifty crosses in a row. Nobody in the squad has done it. The record is thirty-one.

choices.label: Stay every day until you beat it
choices.text: It takes nine days. On day nine he hits fifty-two. The assistant coach writes his name on the whiteboard in permanent marker.

choices.label: Try it once for fun
choices.text: He hits nineteen and laughs. Not bad for a first go.

scenarios.title: Look Over Your Shoulder
scenarios.text: The analyst counts how often he scans before receiving the ball: four times a minute. The best midfielders in the world do it eight times. 'Look more,' says the coach. 'Look before you need to.'

choices.label: Drills with coloured cards and shouted numbers
choices.text: Coaches hold up coloured cards behind him while he receives passes. It's ridiculous. Three weeks later he sees the whole pitch.

choices.label: Watch videos of the best
choices.text: He watches hours of the world's best midfielders. He starts copying the way they move their heads.

scenarios.title: Finishing School
scenarios.text: A retired striker, a club legend with three hundred goals, comes in twice a week to work with the forwards. He watches {J} take ten shots and then says, 'You're thinking. Stop thinking.'

choices.label: Every session he's here
choices.text: He teaches {J} where to look, when to shoot early and how to stay calm when the keeper comes out. Little things. Everything.

choices.label: Ask him about the mental side
choices.text: 'I once went eleven games without a goal,' says the legend. 'On the twelfth I scored three. You are never as bad as the drought says.'

scenarios.title: The Data
scenarios.text: The club's new sports scientist puts a GPS vest on everyone. His data says {J}'s sprints drop by a third after the 70th minute and his sleep is terrible.

choices.label: Overhaul sleep and recovery
choices.desc: Blackout curtains, no phone after ten.
choices.text: No phone after ten, blackout blinds, a sleep coach. His late-match numbers climb within a month.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: He ignores it. The sports scientist shows the manager the graphs anyway.

scenarios.title: No More Fried Food
scenarios.text: The club nutritionist has looked at his food diary and gone quiet. She wants him to cut out fried food, sugar and the late-night snacks he thinks nobody knows about.

choices.label: Follow it strictly
choices.hint: Your body thanks you. Your soul complains.
choices.text: Three miserable weeks, then he feels lighter, sharper and less tired. He still dreams about fried chicken.

choices.label: Mostly follow it, with a cheat day
choices.text: Six days of discipline, one day of joy. It works and he stays sane.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: He ignores it. His body fat numbers go up. So do the nutritionist's eyebrows.

scenarios.title: Yoga
scenarios.text: The fitness coach wants the squad doing yoga twice a week. The senior players laugh. The physio says the hamstring injuries would halve.

choices.label: Commit to it
choices.text: He can't touch his toes in week one. By week ten he's the most flexible player in the squad and the teasing has stopped.

choices.label: Go through the motions
choices.text: He mostly naps in the corpse pose. Not entirely useless.

scenarios.title: Red Numbers
scenarios.text: His training load numbers are flashing red on the sports scientist's screen. 'One more hard week,' she says, 'and something will tear.'
scenarios.prompt: Your body is close to breaking.

choices.label: Take a full rest week
choices.text: He rests. He hates it. A week later the numbers are green and so is he.

out.text: He pushes through, somehow, and the numbers recover. Lucky.

scenarios.title: Dead Balls
scenarios.text: The club's set-piece coach wants a new free-kick taker. The current one is ageing. He's watching {J} curl balls over the wall after training.

choices.label: Practise two hundred a week
choices.text: Two hundred free kicks a week. A month later, he's given the job. The first one he takes in a match hits the bar. The second goes in.

choices.label: Leave it to the veteran
choices.text: He leaves it to the veteran. One day the job will come to him.

scenarios.title: Altitude
scenarios.text: Pre-season camp at altitude: thin air, brutal runs, nothing to do in the evenings but sleep and play cards. Some players love it. Most players hate it.
scenarios.prompt: How do you approach altitude camp?

choices.label: Go all out
choices.text: He wins every run. The coaches love it. On day six, he throws up on a mountain.

choices.label: Pace yourself
choices.text: He finishes strong, not first. Fresh legs for the season.

choices.label: Become the card-game champion
choices.text: He runs the evening card tournament. The squad has never been closer, or poorer.

scenarios.title: An Idea
scenarios.text: Watching the video of the last match, {J} sees something: their left-back always steps up too early. If he drifts wide at the right moment, he's in behind. Should he tell {M}?
scenarios.prompt: Share your tactical idea with the manager?

out.text: {Mf} watches the clip, says nothing, then builds the next week's training around it. They win. {Mf} winks at him on the bus.
{Mf} says, 'I'll do the tactics. You do the running.' Message received.

choices.label: Just do it on the pitch
choices.text: He drifts wide. It works twice. {Mf} asks him afterwards whose idea that was.

scenarios.title: The Manager's Son
scenarios.text: {M}'s son plays in the academy and idolises {J}. {Mf} asks, a little awkwardly, whether {J} would spend an hour with the boy.
scenarios.prompt: Spend time with the manager's son?

choices.label: Spend a whole afternoon
choices.text: He spends the afternoon with the boy, who doesn't stop talking for four hours. {Mf} looks at {J} differently after that.

choices.label: An hour, as asked
choices.text: A good hour. The boy goes home happy.

scenarios.title: Named in the Press Conference
scenarios.text: After the defeat, {M} tells the press that 'some players need to look at themselves'. Then, asked to name them, he names {J}.

choices.label: Accept it and work harder
choices.text: He says nothing, trains harder and plays better the following week. {Mf} praises him in the next press conference.

choices.label: Ask for a private meeting
choices.hint: Fair point, delivered well or badly.

out.text: {Mf} agrees that should have been private. Respect, rebuilt.
{Mf} says he'll say what he likes. The meeting makes it worse.

choices.label: Answer back in the media
choices.text: His reply is the back-page lead. {Mf} drops him for three matches.

scenarios.title: 'He Can Go to the Very Top'
scenarios.text: {M} tells the press that {J} 'can go to the very top'. Agents start calling. Teammates start teasing. His mother frames the newspaper.

choices.label: Stay humble
choices.text: He credits the team. The dressing room approves.

choices.label: Use it as motivation
choices.text: He writes the quote on a sticky note and puts it on his mirror next to the other one.

scenarios.title: Different Ways
scenarios.text: The manager shouts. In {J}'s culture, being shouted at in front of others is humiliating. In the manager's culture, it means he cares. {J} has started to dread training.
scenarios.prompt: The manager's style clashes with your culture.

choices.label: Explain it to {Mf} privately
choices.text: {Mf} listens, surprised. He keeps shouting at everyone else. With {J}, he talks quietly. Things improve.

choices.label: Adapt yourself
choices.text: He learns to hear the care behind the volume. It takes months.

scenarios.title: Double Session
scenarios.text: After a bad result, {M} announces double sessions for a week. Morning and afternoon. The senior players are grumbling about it in the canteen.
scenarios.prompt: How do you respond to the double sessions?

choices.label: Lead from the front
choices.desc: First in, last out, no complaints.
choices.text: He leads every drill. {Mf} notices. Some senior players roll their eyes.

choices.label: Join the grumbling
choices.text: He grumbles with the seniors. The manager hears about it.

scenarios.title: The Clip
scenarios.text: In the video session, the analyst plays the same clip of {J}'s mistake six times. Slow motion. From three angles. The squad watches in silence.
scenarios.prompt: Your mistake is on the big screen.

choices.label: Own it out loud
choices.text: He says it before anyone else can. The silence turns into nods.

choices.label: Explain what happened
choices.text: He explains the context. It sounds like an excuse. Even though it isn't.

scenarios.title: Only Here on Loan
scenarios.text: Some players treat the loan player like a temporary guest. Others treat him like competition. {J} isn't sure if anyone thinks of him as one of the team.
scenarios.prompt: How do you approach life as a loan player?

choices.label: Act like you'll be here forever
choices.text: He commits to everything: the team nights, the charity visits, the club's anthem. By spring, nobody remembers he's on loan.

choices.label: Focus only on minutes
choices.text: He focuses on his own development. It works on the pitch. Off it, he's a stranger.

scenarios.title: The Training-Pitch Champion
scenarios.text: He's been the best player in training for weeks. On matchday, he's on the bench again. One of the coaches whispers, 'Keep going. He sees it.'
scenarios.prompt: You're excelling in training but not playing.

choices.label: Keep going
choices.text: He keeps going. Three weeks later, an injury opens the door and he walks through it.

choices.label: Ask the coach what more you can do
choices.text: The coach says the manager wants more defensive work from him. Specific, fixable, annoying.

choices.label: Let your effort drop
choices.text: His effort drops. The coaches notice instantly. So does the manager.

scenarios.title: A Private Coach
scenarios.text: A famous private performance coach, who works with several superstars, has a slot. He's expensive and intense, and his methods sometimes clash with clubs.

choices.label: Hire him
choices.hint: Gains, maybe friction with the club.

out.text: Twice a week, extra work at 6am. His explosiveness improves. The club's fitness coach is a little jealous.
The private coach's plan clashes with the club's. {J} is overloaded. A tweak in his calf.

choices.label: Trust the club's staff
choices.text: He trusts the club's staff. They appreciate it.

scenarios.title: The Ice Bath
scenarios.text: The ice bath is two degrees. The rule is five minutes. The squad record is twenty-one minutes, held by a centre-back nobody likes.

out.text: Twenty-two minutes. He can't feel his legs. He is a legend.
Fourteen minutes and the physio pulls him out, blue-lipped. Respect for trying.

choices.label: Five minutes, as prescribed
choices.text: Five minutes, out, warm shower. His legs thank him.

scenarios.title: Boxing Gym
scenarios.text: A teammate swears by boxing training for footwork and fitness. There's an old gym downtown run by a former champion who doesn't care who anyone is.

choices.label: Go every week
choices.text: The old champion makes him skip until his calves scream. His footwork sharpens. His ego shrinks.

choices.label: Spar, for real
choices.text: He spars. He takes a punch on the nose. The club physio's face, when he sees it on Monday, is a picture.

scenarios.title: Last Chance
scenarios.text: {M} calls him into his office and shuts the door. 'I'll be honest. You're not in my plans. But I'll give you one match. If you want to stay, show me.'

out.text: He plays like his career depends on it, because it does. {Mf} shakes his hand afterwards and says, 'Okay. Stay.'
Nerves get him. A quiet, forgettable ninety minutes. {Mf} doesn't say anything. He doesn't need to.

choices.label: Say you'd rather leave
choices.text: He thanks {Mf} and asks to be listed. A clean ending to a messy chapter.

scenarios.title: The Captain's Voice
scenarios.text: As captain, {M} asks for {J}'s opinion on the team selection for a big match. It's a privilege and a trap: whatever he says, some teammates will find out.
scenarios.prompt: The manager wants your opinion on selection.

choices.label: Give your honest view
choices.hint: Trust from the manager. Risk with the squad.
choices.text: He gives his honest view, including that a friend should be dropped. The friend is dropped. He never finds out who suggested it.

choices.label: Say selection is the manager's job
choices.text: 'You're the boss.' {Mf} nods, a little disappointed.

scenarios.title: Coaching Badges
scenarios.text: The federation runs a coaching course for current players: evenings and off-days, two years, the first step to managing one day.

choices.label: Sign up
choices.text: Evenings in a classroom with other players and former players. He sees the game differently: as a puzzle, not just a fight.

choices.label: Not yet
choices.text: Not yet. One day.

scenarios.title: The Tackle
scenarios.text: In a training match, {J} goes in hard on {T}. A fair tackle, mostly. {T} doesn't get up. Ankle. The physio is shaking his head.
scenarios.prompt: You hurt a teammate in training.

choices.label: Go to the hospital with him
choices.text: He sits in the waiting room for three hours. {T} is out for a month. He visits every week. They're closer after it.

choices.label: Apologise and keep training
choices.text: He apologises and gets back to work. {T} thinks it was cold. The squad is split.

scenarios.title: A New Position?
scenarios.text: The coaches think {J} could be better somewhere else on the pitch: a different role, a different set of skills. It would mean starting again in some ways.

choices.label: Try it in training
choices.text: Weeks of training in a new role. Some of it works. The coaches decide he's best where he is, but now he understands the game better.

choices.label: Refuse
choices.text: He refuses, politely. The coaches respect a player who knows himself.

scenarios.title: The New System
scenarios.text: Pre-season: the manager is installing a new system. Complicated pressing triggers, new positions, a binder of instructions as thick as a dictionary.
scenarios.prompt: How do you learn the new system?

choices.label: Study the binder at home
choices.text: He studies it like a law student. By the first match he's explaining it to teammates.

choices.label: Learn it on the pitch
choices.text: He learns it by doing. Slower, but it sticks.

scenarios.title: The Assistant Coach
scenarios.text: The assistant coach, a quiet former defender, has started staying after training to work with {J} one-on-one. He doesn't say why. He just keeps turning up.

choices.label: Every day he offers
choices.text: Six months of extra sessions. He improves in ways nobody can quite explain. The assistant becomes a friend for life.

choices.label: Ask him why
choices.text: 'You remind me of me,' he says. 'Except you can still do something about it.'

scenarios.title: Contract Year
scenarios.text: His contract is up at the end of the season. Every training session feels like an audition, for this club or another one.
scenarios.prompt: How do you handle a contract year?

choices.label: Ignore it and play
choices.desc: The football takes care of it.
choices.text: He blocks it out. His football speaks. The phone starts ringing.

choices.label: Train like it's the last year of your life
choices.text: He trains like a man possessed. His numbers are the best they've ever been. So is his stress.

scenarios.title: The Scales
scenarios.text: Pre-season weigh-in. Some players have clearly enjoyed their holidays. The manager reads the numbers out loud, in front of everyone.

choices.label: You trained all summer
choices.text: He's two kilos lighter than last season. {Mf} reads it out with a nod.

choices.label: You enjoyed yourself
choices.text: Three kilos heavier. The squad cheers sarcastically. Double sessions for a week.

scenarios.title: The Rehab Room
scenarios.text: {T} is injured too. For weeks, they're the only two in the rehab gym: same exercises, same boredom, same fear of not coming back as good.

choices.label: Push each other
choices.text: Every exercise is a competition. They come back within a week of each other, best friends.

choices.label: Keep to yourself
choices.text: He keeps to himself, headphones in. The weeks drag.

scenarios.title: Dropped for No Reason
scenarios.text: He's been the best player for a month. Then he's dropped, without explanation. The assistant coach whispers that the manager does this 'to keep players hungry'.
scenarios.prompt: The manager is playing mind games.

choices.label: Play the game: train harder
choices.hint: He wants a reaction. Give him one.
choices.text: He trains like an animal all week. He's back in the team on Saturday and scores. {Mf} smiles for the first time all season.

choices.label: Demand an explanation
choices.text: {Mf} says he doesn't owe explanations. Then, a week later, he gives one anyway.
